Subject: Aligning Forecast Buckets + 20-min micro-training (action: update stages this week)

Team — quick note and an ask for this week's cleanup work before our quarter wrap. Finance ran a brief audit and found several deals in the "Best Case" bucket that either don't have an updated close plan or are still technically in early evaluation (informal POC). To keep our Q3 forecast sane we need a short alignment:

- What I'm changing: clarifying definitions for the three forecast buckets we use (Commit / Best Case / Pipeline) and providing canonical examples so reps make consistent choices.
- Ask: please review any open opportunities you own and move any that match the new definitions by end-of-day Friday. If you disagree on a bucket, note why in the opportunity comments and flag me.
- Training: I scheduled two 20-minute micro-training slots (Wed 10:00am PT and Thu 3:00pm PT) focused on borderline cases and common redlines — attendance requested for AE + AMs owning deals > $50k.

Attached: pipeline-buckets-guidelines-v2.pdf (short cheat-sheet) and commit-examples-keeper.xlsx (10 anonymized examples with guidance). Also linking the Drive folder so you can comment.

Why this matters: Finance needs tighter signal to model run scenarios for capacity planning; inaccurate buckets are causing our forecast to swing ~6-8% in scenario sims. Small hygiene wins here materially reduce churn on the final numbers.

If there are account-specific concerns (Apex, Globex, etc.), loop in the appropriate CS lead and I'll coordinate.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Head of Growth Ops, Redwood Inference

Jordan — thanks for the heads up and for including Apex. A quick clarification from our side: procurement confirmation for us is typically the PO and the initial SOW being agreed; legal review can lag. From your definitions, it sounds like that would be Commit. If that lines up with your guidance, the deal owner will move it accordingly.

We appreciate the short training sessions — Ben, I'll try to join the Q&A if helpful.

—Emma

Emma — exactly right, thanks. If procurement has provided a PO or written commitment to purchase (even if legal redlines remain), treat that as Commit. The cheat-sheet has a short decision flow to make this deterministic.

Ben — to your earlier point on POC vs. procurement: if a POC will lead to procurement only after a successful technical signoff, keep it in Pipeline/Best Case until the procurement step is explicit (documented email or Jira ticket).

Logistics: Wed 10am PT session link: https://meet.redwoodinference.com/rooms/micro-train-0324 (recording will be posted). I've also dropped a one-slide decision tree into the Drive link. Please update opportunities and add a one-sentence reason any time you move a deal bucket (helps audit later).

Attachments: pipeline-buckets-guidelines-v2.pdf (updated minor language)

Jordan
